_meta.purpose: Immutable, append-only ledger of pre-committed LOVS methodology calibration points for the BDBV 2026 outbreak. Each block is a pin moment: a set of corridors committed on a fixed date, with a fixed model uncertainty range and a fixed resolution date. refresh_pipeline.py reads the active (unresolved) blocks and carries their points forward UNCHANGED into every snapshot; it never re-derives them from the current run's corridor ranking. That carry-forward is the pre-commitment contract the calibration scoring depends on.
doctrine: Pin once. A block's points, model ranges, pin date, and resolution date are never edited after commit.
Carry forward. A daily refresh re-emits the active points verbatim. Re-deriving them from freshly ranked corridors would silently overwrite an earlier commitment and break pre-commitment.
Append only. New calibration points are added as a NEW block at an explicit pin moment, never by mutating an existing block.
Resolve by appending. On a resolution date, score the due points against public reports and append the outcome; the original pinned range is never altered.

Early-lock when monotonic-safe. A point may have its outcome appended before its block's resolves_at iff a new lab-confirmed case appears in the target zone strictly inside [pinned_at, resolves_at]: the YES outcome is monotonic-safe (cannot flip back) and the append is structurally identical to a resolution-date append. The early-lock authorization applies only to YES outcomes; resolved_no outcomes wait for resolves_at to remove ambiguity about late-arriving evidence.
_meta.id_derivation: hypothesis_id = 'calibration-point:bdbv-uga-cod-2026:30d:' + sha256('bdbv-uga-cod-2026|{source}|{target}|{horizon_days}d|{pinned_at}')[:10]. refresh_pipeline._calibration_point_id reproduces this and verifies every point's id against its corridor at load time.

blocks.rationale: Fourth calibration block. Pins the 2026-06-04 west/SSD corridor expansion: two new candidate targets (yei-ssd, kisangani-cod) graduate to pinned corridor endpoints, and the four highest-signal source-to-target corridors to them are committed at the ascertainment-adjusted 50% intervals from the 2026-06-04 pipeline run with both targets added to candidate_target_zones. yei-ssd tests northward cross-border exportation to South Sudan (West Nile / Morobo-Kaya axis); kisangani-cod tests the westward Tshopo / Congo-river axis (RN4 via Mambasa and Bafwasende), a no-PCR surveillance gap. The aru -> yei-ssd point is a designed geography-vs-load blindspot probe (frontier geography flags Aru while the case-load model rates it low). Corridor basis: WHO DON603 (2026-05-29). blocks.rationale: Block 5. First block pinned since 2026-07-05, closing a 58-day gap in which the outbreak grew from 35 to 60 affected health zones and 6,041 confirmed cases with zero open forward commitments (public_nowcast_status.json recorded open_calibration_commitments: 0). Pre-registration cannot be backfilled, so that gap is permanent; this block restarts the clock. WHAT THIS BLOCK TESTS: whether the corridor model is still calibrated at all. At the current burden the model's target-level hazard has saturated. For every one of the six eligible targets the union hazard across all 60 affected source zones is 1.000000, and even the single strongest corridor into each target reads 0.9994 to 0.9999. The model is asserting, with effective certainty, that all six targets record a first in-window confirmation within 30 days. Two of those targets make that implausible on its face: South Sudan has reported no confirmed case in 3.5 months of exposure, and WHO declared Uganda's outbreak over on 2026-08-26. This block pins that assertion at the model's own value so it is decided by the world rather than argued about. At p about 0.9997 a single NO is an unambiguous falsification carrying a Brier penalty near 1.0, which makes this the most information-dense experiment the corridor ledger can run. The six targets are heterogeneous, so WHICH of them fire is diagnostic of what the model is missing even though the six pinned probabilities are alike. This block is deliberately single-bin. Spanning probability bands, the design this block was first drafted with, is not deliverable from this model against this evidence feed, and attempting it produces a false result -- see registration_note.
blocks.registration_note: Pinned 2026-09-01 on founder go-signal, NOT backdated. Model values are read verbatim from data/live-bdbv-2026-output.json (as_of 2026-08-29T23:59:59Z, data_as_of 2026-08-29); no probability in this block is authored. REVISED PRE-PUBLICATION, same pin date, after a second-pass review and before any push or public release. The first draft pinned 12 points selected across six probability bands, two per band. That design was wrong and would have produced a fabricated result. The resolution evidence feed (data/calibration-resolution-evidence.json) is keyed by TARGET ZONE and carries one confirmed_in_window boolean per target, so every pin sharing a target resolves from the SAME event. The 12 points covered only 6 distinct targets, making half of them redundant; and a low-band pin such as 'kambala -> bundibugyo-uga' at 0.023 states P(export via that one source), which is not the quantity the feed resolves. The model's belief about the resolvable event is the union, 1.000000. Scoring 0.023 against a target-level outcome would have measured the model against a claim it never made and manufactured evidence of low-end miscalibration. The same flaw is present, unnoticed, in Blocks 2, 3 and 4: yei-ssd was scored at both 0.022 and 0.561 for one event, and goma-cod three times for one event. Blocks 1 to 4 carry 19 points but only 12 distinct target-events. Block 5 therefore pins ONE point per eligible target: six independent events, each at the strongest corridor hazard the model emits into that target, with the full target-level union recorded alongside in target_union_hazard_50. LOOK-AHEAD AUDIT. Targets already carrying a confirmed case are excluded as saturated: beni-cod (136 confirmed), goma-cod (1), kisangani-cod (9, first confirmation 2026-06-30). Uganda targets are eligible because only a confirmation dated inside [pinned_at, resolves_at] resolves a point YES, so the pre-window Uganda caseload of 20 is excluded by construction. RESIDUAL RISK, stated rather than hidden: the model snapshot is data_as_of 2026-08-29 against a 2026-09-01 pin, a three-day lag, audited against the 2026-08-31 ECDC update, which showed no new Uganda or South Sudan case. Any point later found to have been pre-resolved must be retired in a dated note, never silently rescored.
